name: IEC odd-parity element
summary: Element marked 2k+1 that is active when an odd number of inputs are active, as used for parity.
description: The 2k+1 qualifier means the output is active when an odd number of inputs are active. It is what a cascade of two-input exclusive-OR gates actually computes, and it is the correct IEC qualifier for an odd-parity tree drawn as a single element.

Drafters converting older drawings sometimes mark a multi-input parity tree as =1. That is wrong under the IEC meaning, because =1 requires exactly one active input. Replacing it with 2k+1 removes the ambiguity.
The element does not indicate the number of data bits on its own; show the full input set or a grouped bus with its width.
readingNotes: Do not read 2k+1 as exactly one active.
Check whether the result is used as odd or even parity downstream.
drawingChecklist: Reference the parity convention used by the protocol or memory.
distinction: The =1 element gives the same result only for two inputs.
